newsitem.title: UK: May Brent loadings up at 41.8 cargoes, inc top-ups.
newsitem.headline: May Brent loadings up at 41.8 cargoes, inc top-ups.

text.p: The May North Sea Brent Blend crude oil loading programme has been set at the equivalent of 41.8 cargoes, made up of 39 full 500,000-barrel cargoes, plus 1.43 million barrels in top-ups, traders said on Tuesday.
The May programme scheduled the equivalent of two full cargoes more than the revised programme for April, when 37 full cargoes plus 1.4 million barrels were due to load.

Traders said the higher programme was due to the longer month and a slightly lighter maintenance schedule on the Brent system than in April, when Chevron's 50,000 barrels per day (bpd) Ninian field and Texaco's 40,000 bpd Strathspey were both closed for about 12 days.

Long-term maintenance at Shell Expro's 55,000 bpd Brent Delta platform, which began on April 1, will continue through May and there will also be a week-long shutdown at Shell Expro's 17,000 bpd Eider field.
Crude from the Brent and Ninian systems is blended at the Sullom Voe terminal on the Shetland Islands and exported as world benchmark Brent Blend.
Shell Exploration and Production (Shell Expro) is a joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Exxon Corp.
